parameters.query:
-- The sources that are due, and a collection_runs row for each, in one step.
-- A run that dies halfway still leaves its started row behind.
--
-- The editors choose the times from Telegram with /schedule, kept in
-- app_settings.collection_times as "08:00 14:00" or "off". A source is due once
-- the latest of those times has passed since it was last checked. /check and
-- POST /collect skip this and check everything now.
--
-- last_checked_at is set when a check starts, so the next tick does not start
-- the same source again while it is still running.
--
-- rss and crossref sources go to the Feed collector. The only webpage collector
-- is the crawler for the client's own site, so another webpage source waits
-- until someone writes a reader for it.
WITH slot AS (
    SELECT max(d + t::time) AS last_slot          -- Finnish local time
      FROM app_settings,
           regexp_split_to_table(value, ' ') AS t,
           (VALUES ((now() AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::date),
                   ((now() AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::date - 1)) AS days(d)
     WHERE key = 'collection_times'
       AND t ~ '^[0-9]{1,2}:[0-9]{2}$'
       AND d + t::time <= now() AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki'
),
due AS (
    SELECT id, url, type, fetch_full_text, publisher
      FROM sources
     WHERE active
       AND (type IN ('rss', 'crossref')
            OR (type = 'webpage' AND url LIKE 'https://eoppimiskeskus.fi/%'))
       AND ($1::boolean
            OR (SELECT last_slot FROM slot) > coalesce(last_checked_at AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki', '-infinity'))
     ORDER BY id
       FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
),
started AS (
    INSERT INTO collection_runs (source_id)
    SELECT id FROM due
    RETURNING id AS run_id, source_id
),
touched AS (
    UPDATE sources s SET last_checked_at = now()
      FROM due WHERE s.id = due.id
)
SELECT st.run_id, d.id AS source_id, d.url, d.type, d.fetch_full_text, d.publisher
  FROM started st
  JOIN due d ON d.id = st.source_id
 ORDER BY d.id;

UPDATE collection_runs
   SET finished_at = now(),
       items_found = $2::int,
       items_new   = $3::int,
       error       = nullif($4, '')
 WHERE id = $1::bigint
RETURNING id, source_id, items_found, items_new, error;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('One at a time').first().json.run_id, $json.items_found || 0, $json.items_new || 0, ($json.error && ($json.error.message || $json.error)) || ($json.items_found === undefined ? 'the collector returned nothing' : '') ] }}

parameters.query:
-- What the person who asked for the check is told. Runs once, after the last
-- source, and only reads what the runs above wrote.
WITH runs AS (
    SELECT r.*, s.name
      FROM collection_runs r
      JOIN sources s ON s.id = r.source_id
     WHERE r.id = ANY (string_to_array($1, ',')::bigint[])
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM runs)::int                        AS sources,
       (SELECT coalesce(sum(items_found), 0) FROM runs)::int    AS found,
       (SELECT coalesce(sum(items_new), 0) FROM runs)::int      AS new,
       (SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(name || ': ' || error), '[]'::jsonb)
          FROM runs WHERE error IS NOT NULL)                     AS problems,
       (SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(i.title ORDER BY i.id), '[]'::jsonb)
          FROM items i
         WHERE i.source_id IN (SELECT source_id FROM runs)
           AND i.created_at >= (SELECT min(started_at) FROM runs)) AS new_titles;

-- The run row was made when the whole check began. This is when this source's
-- turn came, so collection_runs shows how long each source really took.
UPDATE collection_runs r
   SET started_at = now()
  FROM sources s
 WHERE r.id = $1::bigint
   AND s.id = r.source_id
RETURNING r.id AS run_id, s.id AS source_id, s.url, s.type, s.fetch_full_text, s.publisher;
